name: LIC & Life Insurance Policies
tagline: Cover and savings in one contract.
blurb: Life insurance policies from LIC and its GIFT City branch. A policy mixes two things that are priced separately elsewhere: a death benefit, and a savings or pension component. The premium depends on your age, the term and the sum assured, so it is never a single number.
whatToCheck: What the policy pays if you die, and when
What you get back if you survive the term — and what you get if you stop paying
The surrender value after each year, and how long the money is actually locked
Whether a term plan plus a separate investment would do the same job for less

name: Government & Post Office Schemes
tagline: Small savings run by the state.
blurb: Savings certificates, deposits and pensions offered through post offices and government bodies. Tenures are usually fixed, the rate is notified by the government and revised every quarter, and early exit is often restricted.
whatToCheck: The rate for this quarter, and that it is reset at the start of each quarter
The lock-in, and what happens if you close early
Who can open it — age, relationship or income limits

name: Bank Savings & Fixed Deposits
blurb: Savings accounts and fixed deposits at scheduled banks. Deposits are insured up to a limit by the DICGC, and the interest you earn is contractual — but it can be lower than inflation, and early withdrawal usually costs you.
whatToCheck: Whether the rate is fixed or floats with a reference rate
Premature withdrawal penalties and notice periods
Whether the bank is insured and how much cover applies

name: Mutual Funds
tagline: Pooled money, managed to a stated mandate.
blurb: Professionally managed pools of stocks, bonds or both. There is no promised return: the value of your units moves with the underlying holdings, and the fund's mandate — not a guarantee — decides what it can hold.
whatToCheck: What the scheme actually holds, and how concentrated it is
The expense ratio and exit load
Whether a lock-in applies, and the fund's benchmark

name: Government Bonds & Fixed-Income
tagline: Lending money for a stated interest.
blurb: You lend to a government or a company, which pays interest and returns the principal on a set date. Government issues carry the least credit risk; corporate bonds pay more because the borrower may fail. Prices move if you sell before maturity.
whatToCheck: Who the borrower is, and what happens if they default
Whether you plan to hold to maturity or sell early
The yield, which is not the same as the coupon

name: ETFs & Market-Linked Products
tagline: Bought on an exchange, priced by the market.
blurb: Exchange-traded funds and similar products track an index, a commodity or a basket. They trade like shares during market hours, so the price you get depends on the market at that moment — not on a value fixed at the end of the day.
whatToCheck: What the product tracks, and how closely it has done so
The expense ratio and the bid-ask spread
Whether the price can differ from the value of what it holds
